FAST

MUNICH, Oct 31 : Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post for Bayern Munich as Borussia Dortmund snatched a last-gasp equaliser through Fabio Silva for a 2-2 draw in the Klassiker on Saturday that kept the teams level on points at the top. Kane, who won his prize in a ceremony in London on Monday, was an unused substitute in the 6-1 German Cup second-round demolition of Magdeburg on Wednesday before missing from the spot with Bayern 1-0 up. He also hit the post, one of four times Bayern hit the woodwork. Silva snatched the equaliser in the 89th minute to leave both teams on 18 points, with Bayern top on goal difference. In a rollercoaster first half Bayern hit the woodwork through Michael Olise and missed a golden chance for Ismael Saibari, who was injured in the process, before the visitors had a goal overruled by VAR.

Bayern, also hit by injuries to Serge Gnabry and Olise, struck in the 38th thanks through Konrad Laimer's goal on the rebound, after his first effort was blocked by Dortmund's Gregor Kobel. With Bayern coach Vincent Kompany recovering after his collapse last week, Bayern's full back Laimer was more threatening than Kane, who sent his 56th minute spot-kick against the crossbar. Dortmund scored through Serhou Guirassy on the hour mark but their joy only lasted six minutes as Dayot Upamecano tapped in a Kane assist from close range. Kane's low shot bounced off the post before Silva bagged the equaliser. Bayern's Lennart Karl still had time to see his shot in stoppage time bounce off the crossbar and cap a frustrating day for the champions.

Source: Reuters

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Reigning champion Lando Norris was fastest on Saturday in final practice for a Mexico City Grand Prix set to crown 20-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli as Formula One's youngest title winner. The McLaren driver put in a flying late lap of one minute 17.600 seconds at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez to top the timesheets by the slimmest of margins, 0.001 faster than Antonelli who is poised to become Italy's first F1 world champion since 1953. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, fastest in both Friday sessions, was third quickest and 0.117 off the pace, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri fourth. Red Bull's four-times champion Max Verstappen, who has a one place grid drop for Sunday's race, was fifth fastest ahead of Ferrari's seven-times champion Lewis Hamilton.

Antonelli will be champion if he finishes ninth or higher. Japan's Ryo Hirakawa, replacing Frenchman Esteban Ocon at Haas and set for his F1 debut at the age of 32, was 19th fastest.  Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto and Cadillac's home hero Sergio Perez failed to set any timed laps, with both having changes of their cars' power units ahead of qualifying.

By Rohith Nair Oct 31 : MotoGP is set to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix even as a group of riders demand more assurances for travelling to the region, with organisers arguing that a "zero-risk environment" is unrealistic. The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to November 6-8 due to the regional conflict.

"MotoGP has provided teams and riders with every assurance available from the State of Qatar, the circuit... and our own ongoing risk assessment processes," a MotoGP spokesperson told Reuters. "We fully respect the concerns raised and highlight that safety remains the priority for everyone involved." However, the spokesperson said the expectation of a zero-risk environment was not realistic anywhere in the world by any government or organiser. "Over the past months, we have maintained continuous dialogue with teams and riders, sharing the latest information available, providing direct access to documents and answering questions openly and transparently." Carlos Ezpeleta, deputy CEO of MotoGP, visited Qatar on Thursday where the circuit's president Abdulrahman Al-Mannai said they were ready to welcome the riders, teams and fans for the 20th round of the season. However, Spain's embassy in Qatar has issued a notice urging its citizens not to travel to the Gulf nation unless it was absolutely necessary. Spaniards make up the largest share of riders on the grid, including world champion Marc Marquez. EVACUATION PLAN IN PLACE A MotoGP source said Qatar has guaranteed teams would not be stranded in case of escalation in the conflict and they could leave the country safely in time for the final two rounds in Portugal and Spain later in November. "Additional impossible asks at the last moment go beyond what can realistically be guaranteed by any event organiser, government or sporting body," the spokesperson added. "Our position is based solely on the most up-to-date intelligence, expert advice and assurances available to us." RIDERS SEEK ASSURANCES The source said championship leader Marquez, a seven-times MotoGP champion, was one of the riders seeking more assurances. Marquez has not publicly stated his position on travelling to Qatar but Ducati team manager Davide Tardozzi defended the Spaniard after he came under criticism for not taking a stance. "I have read that all the blame has been placed on Marc, as if he were the one who did not want to go to Qatar. That is not the case," he told Sky Sport. "Marc simply asked, as many other riders did, for an organisational safety plan - nothing more, nothing less. He did not say, 'I don't want to go'. "There are circumstances that could make you think it would be better not to go. But if the necessary safety conditions are in place, including an evacuation plan and guarantees that there will be no problems if something happens, then we will go." Reuters has contacted Ducati and Marquez for comment. APRILIA KEEN TO RACE IN QATAR Aprilia are keen to race in Qatar with Spanish rider Jorge Martin, second in the standings behind Marquez after withdrawing from the Malaysian Grand Prix due to a wrist injury. "We need to turn the page and look to the next chapter, Qatar, hoping it goes better, and keep this fight going to the last," Aprilia's technical director Fabiano Sterlacchini said. "This setback has certainly made things harder for us." The MotoGP source confirmed that no decision has been taken about sporting sanctions if teams or riders do not participate in Qatar.

Source: Reuters

Oct 31 : Manchester City slumped to their second Premier League defeat in a row on Saturday, going down 1-0 at home to third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion thanks to an early goal by Yasin Ayari. City could be knocked off their perch at the top of the table if Arsenal get at least a point at Liverpool on Sunday. The defeat was City's first at home by Brighton in the Premier League, and though Enzo Maresca's side managed 21 shots on goal, only six were on target and none managed to beat keeper Bart Verbruggen.  "Unbelievable feeling. We go 1-0 up and then to hang tight, the last 30-40 minutes we completely lost control of the game," Verbruggen told Sky Sports.

"The manager said this morning we have to dig deep and that's what we did. So happy to get over the line and can't wait to celebrate with the boys." City remained top on 21 points, ahead of Arsenal on goal difference, and Brighton remain third on 19 points after six wins and a draw in their opening nine games.  "(We're) just focusing every day on what's ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season," Verbruggen said.  City's star-studded attack struggled, with giant Norwegian striker Erling Haaland looking a shadow of himself as his run of scoring in seven successive Premier League games ended.  "We created a lot of chances, disappointing to lose. Didn't manage to put chances away, on another day we put three or four away," City midfielder Elliot Anderson said.  "We're all disappointed. Not good enough, we don't want to be losing games but we've got to stick together - we've had a great start to the season, two disappointing results now, but we have to stick together."

Source: Reuters

FAST

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar was given a formal warning on Saturday after he pushed away a Formula One guest in the Mexico City Grand Prix paddock. • The Frenchman was hurrying to first practice on Friday but stopped to have a photograph with a young fan when he was approached by a man in what stewards, who summoned Hadjar to a hearing, said was an "aggressive manner". • "One security person was walking behind him and was unable to intervene and prevent what was tantamount to an invasion of the driver's private space," the stewards said. • "The driver initially resisted the move by placing his hand on the waist of the guest, holding him at bay, then the driver pushed him aside with his open right hand." • The stewards said Hadjar was in breach of the regulations but considered various factors in mitigation, including that the action was uninvited and aggressive, that the driver did not have sufficient security and that others had experienced issues in moving through the paddock.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Oct 31 : Fakhar Zaman's superb century powered Pakistan to a three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-Day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday, ending the hosts' long wait for the title. Zaman's 127 off 99 balls anchored the chase after an early wobble, while Salman Agha provided crucial support before Arafat Minhas' half-century paved the way for victory. Pakistan chasing down a target of 326, finished on 331 with nine balls to spare to complete the joint-highest successful chase in an ODI final. Earlier, Sri Lanka posted a formidable 325 for eight wickets, built around Kamindu Mendis' outstanding 131 off 128 balls and a fluent 77 from Pavan Rathnayake. The pair shared a crucial 146-run partnership before Pakistan struck late to curb any hopes of a 340-plus surge, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking two wickets for 50 runs.

The victory secured Pakistan's first ODI tri-series title since 2008, when they beat India in the Kitply Cup final in Bangladesh, and made amends for their defeat to New Zealand in the final of a home tri-series in 2025. Pakistan suffered early setbacks as Dilshan Madushanka struck twice in the powerplay, including the prized wicket of Babar Azam for a five-ball duck. Zaman and Saad Baig rebuilt the innings with an impressive 149-run partnership and Baig brought up his maiden ODI fifty before Maheesh Theekshana ended his knock for 74 off 75 balls. Zaman accelerated after reaching his half-century and went on to register his 12th ODI century, partnering with Agha in a brisk 57-run stand that kept Pakistan firmly on course in the chase. The left-hander eventually fell to Madushanka, followed soon by Agha for 17, leaving Pakistan at 230-5. However, Minhas' and Hasan Nawaz's 94-run partnership ultimately carried the hosts to the target. Sri Lanka made a strong start after being put in to bat, with opener Avishka Fernando and Kamindu Mendis adding 51 runs in the powerplay. Fernando's dismissal in the 18th over ended the opening stand, and Pakistan struck again soon after when captain Kusal Mendis fell to Agha, leaving the visitors at 109-2. Kamindu and Rathnayake steadied the innings with a fluent 146-run partnership off 119 deliveries. The stand kept Sri Lanka firmly in control until Kamindu, who brought up his maiden ODI century, fell after hitting 12 fours and two sixes. Pakistan fought back in the death overs, triggering a collapse as Afridi and Haris Rauf removed Dasun Shanaka and Rathnayake within the space of two overs. Sahan Arachchige provided a late cameo with a brisk 15 off 12 deliveries before falling to Naseem Shah.

Source: Reuters

FAST

LONDON, Oct 31 : Manchester United's nightmare winless run reached nine games when they lost 2-0 at Chelsea and Manchester City also suffered a harrowing Halloween as the Premier League leaders went down 1-0 at home to Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday. United were the better team before halftime at Stamford Bridge but paid heavily for not taking chances as a solo effort by Morgan Rogers and a Cole Palmer penalty after the break heaped more pressure on the visitors' manager Michael Carrick. A horror start to the second half for United was compounded by a needless red card for defender Lisandro Martinez in conceding the 63rd-minute penalty that Palmer tucked away. United were spared dropping into the relegation zone only by virtue of Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace both losing - 2-0 at Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur respectively.

City's 100 per cent Premier League record was ended last week by Aston Villa and their hopes of bouncing back quickly were undone by third-placed Brighton who avenged their midweek League Cup loss to City thanks to Yasin Ayari's early goal. FOREST'S POOR FORM CONTINUES Champions Arsenal will replace City as leaders if they avoid defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. City have 21 points from nine games with Arsenal also on 21 from eight, Brighton on 19 and Chelsea in fourth place on 16. Coventry City moved out of the relegation zone as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni were on target in a 3-1 home win over Sunderland who are bottom. Bournemouth beat Leeds United 2-0 to move seventh with Evanilson netting for the fourth successive league game while Forest remain in the bottom three as their poor form under new manager Oliver Glasner continued with defeat at Brentford making it five league games without a win. The battle between two of the promoted sides ended honours even as Hull City drew 2-2 at home to Ipswich Town. Carrick has now overseen United's longest winless run since 1988 and a fourth successive Premier League defeat means they have just seven points from their opening nine games. Despite the stark statistics, Carrick was warmly applauded by the travelling fans after the final whistle. Bruno Fernandes returned to the starting line-up as captain after being benched for last week's defeat at Bournemouth for his critical comments about the team, and United were rejuvenated as they enjoyed the better of the first half. Things could have been so different had Matheus Cunha's goal been allowed to stand or a host of opportunities been taken, including Amad firing over when looking odds on to score. United's good work unravelled after the break, however, with defender Martinez, who also criticised the club's hierarchy, most culpable. After Rogers strolled through unopposed to dink in Chelsea's opener, Martinez received two yellow cards in three minutes, the second for inexplicably pushing his arm into the face of Wesley Fofana at a corner, to concede the penalty. "I think I take away a lot of the positives from the first half," Carrick said.  "But the game unravelled and got away from us. It's happened too often really so we've got to learn from that and we've got to do something about it pretty quickly." NO GOALS FOR CITY DESPITE 21 ATTEMPTS City had done an impressive job of ignoring the dark clouds hanging over the club after an independent commission found them guilty of 114 out of 115 financial charges but after winning their opening seven Premier League games, Enzo Maresca's side have hit the buffers. They fell behind in the 11th minute when a miscued clearance by Matheus Nunes fell for Ayari who converted from close range. City poured on the pressure in search of an equaliser but Brighton, who had led twice against City in the League Cup, produced a textbook away display to hang on to the points. The hosts had 21 goal attempts but failed to score for the first time in 25 Premier League matches. Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton side have now beaten Arsenal and City this season and while they have been free-scoring, they showed another side on Saturday. "There's an old phrase - defence wins you battles and wins you championships. Of course, we're not speaking about the championship, but especially today we needed to have this defensive mindset. It's always a togetherness when you defend like we did," Hurzeler said. Resurgent Tottenham made it three wins on the bounce to move eighth although they were given a helping hand as Palace had Jean-Philippe Mateta red-carded in the 13th minute for a lunging tackle on Micky van de Ven. Archie Gray headed Spurs in front after 25 minutes and Jan Paul van Hecke wrapped it up in the 73rd minute with a header from a prone position after his initial effort had hit the bar.

Source: Reuters

FSB says US warned Russia of possible Moscow attack

Reuters

31 October, 2026 10:30 pm IST

MOSCOW, Oct 31 (Reuters) – Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) said it had received information from the United States through established partner channels about preparations for a terrorist attack in Moscow and was taking appropriate measures.

The US Embassy in Moscow said separately it was “aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event” on Saturday at Moscow’s Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve and that the US government was coordinating with Russian authorities.

The Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, a palace museum and park complex south of Moscow, has been temporarily closed and access to the park is currently restricted, the RIA news agency reported, citing Russian law enforcement agencies.

Show Full Article

In March 2024, the US Embassy warned that extremists had imminent plans for an attack in Moscow. Days later, gunmen attacked the Crocus City Hall concert venue outside Moscow, killing more than 140 people.

(Reporting by Anton Kolodyazhnyy; Editing by Joe Bavier and Jan Harvey)

Oct 31 : Carlos Alcaraz defeated Daniil Medvedev 6-4 7-6(2) on Saturday to reach the Vienna Open final for the first time, with the Spaniard joined by Australian Alex de Minaur who upset Alexander Zverev. Alcaraz reached the 37th tour-level final of his career and his fifth final of the year while extending his ATP 500 winning streak to 25 matches. The second seed took the opening set after Medvedev double-faulted to hand him set point, but the Russian responded strongly in the second to force a tiebreak. With neither player able to gain a decisive advantage, Alcaraz produced a barrage of powerful groundstrokes in the breaker to seal victory in 96 minutes.

The result gave Alcaraz a measure of revenge after Medvedev handed him his first defeat of the season in the Indian Wells semi-finals in March, and ended the Russian's seven-match winning streak. Both players are among the four men who have already qualified for next month's ATP Finals. De Minaur earned one of the biggest wins of his career, defeating world number one elect Zverev 6-4 1-6 7-6(4) to reach the Vienna final for the first time. The Australian improved to 10-0 indoors this season, kept alive his hopes of qualifying for next month's ATP Finals and advanced to the 23rd tour-level final of his career. De Minaur halted Zverev's winning run and denied the German a place in the final days after it was confirmed he would move top of the world rankings on Monday. Alcaraz and De Minaur will meet in Sunday's final.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Binance recupera el 90% de las criptomonedas robadas y promete reactivar retiros el domingo
item.description: La mayor plataforma de intercambio de criptomonedas del mundo avanzó en la recuperación de los fondos robados y reiteró que los clientes no asumirán el impacto financiero del ataque.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Weeks
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Binance ha afirmado que ha recuperado aproximadamente el 90% de las criptomonedas, por valor de US$6.300 millones, que los piratas informáticos robaron a principios de esta semana, y tiene previsto restablecer las retiradas de fondos para el domingo, lo que supone un avance en su compromiso de reembolsar íntegramente a los clientes. En una publicación en redes sociales el sábado, la mayor plataforma de intercambio de criptomonedas del mundo reiteró que asumirá íntegramente las consecuencias del robo para que los usuarios no sufran ninguna pérdida. Ver más: Hackeo a Binance 2026: qué es el fondo SAFU y cómo cubrirá las pérdidas de los usuarios a nivel global Binance ha estado recuperando diversos tokens con los que huyeron los piratas informáticos, desde Bitcoin hasta Zcash, pasando por las monedas estables USDT y USDC, utilizando una combinación de fondos procedentes de su tesorería corporativa, así como de fondos de emergencia y de seguros. “Binance asumirá el impacto financiero de los fondos sustraídos, no los usuarios”, indicaba la publicación. Los tokens afectados restantes son menos líquidos, lo que dificulta su sustitución. En su anterior actualización, la empresa indicó que había cubierto el 80% de los fondos sustraídos. El ataque a Binance es el mayor de la historia de las criptomonedas, así como uno de los mayores incidentes cibernéticos en general, según los expertos. Ha conmocionado al sector, que ha estado tratando de lograr una mayor aceptación por parte del público general. Binance suspendió las retiradas de fondos como parte de sus medidas de mitigación y afirmó que tiene previsto restablecer la posibilidad de que los clientes recuperen sus fondos a más tardar el domingo. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Japanese reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa will make his Formula One debut in place of Esteban Ocon at US-owned Haas for this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the Formula One team said on Saturday. A team spokesman said the replacement was not due to illness but gave no further details. The governing FIA confirmed the change. There was no immediate comment from Ocon. The French driver is due to leave Haas at the end of the season, with Brazilian Rafael Camara moving up from Formula Two for 2027.

Hirakawa, 32, is a two-times world endurance champion and Le Mans 24 Hours winner with Toyota, who have a technical partnership with Ferrari-powered Haas. He took part in first practice at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Friday, the third time he has done that this season. Haas are seventh in the constructors' championship and seven points ahead of Audi. Britain's Ollie Bearman has scored 23 of their 30 points from 18 races so far. With five races remaining, Ocon's replacement and the lack of further explanation raised questions about who would partner Bearman after Mexico. The next race is the Brazilian Grand Prix in Sao Paulo, a home round for Camara who leads the F2 championship but has no scheduled races until the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi at the end of November and early December. Haas also have Australian Jack Doohan, a former Alpine race driver, as a reserve.  Ocon's future in Formula One remains uncertain, with Cadillac and Racing Bulls the only teams with possible openings but with clear candidates other than the Frenchman. Haas team boss Ayao Komatsu spoke out on Friday about reports that he and Ocon had argued at the Miami Grand Prix in May. "Some people invent the story. You know, what happened in Miami, about apparently I had an argument with Esteban Ocon? That's just absolutely zero truth in there," he said. "Even those people claiming that they had some insider information, etcetera, absolute total nonsense." A tetchy radio exchange between Ocon and his race engineer Laura Mueller in second Friday practice was also highlighted by some, with the driver complaining about the team's decision to switch him to the medium tyre. "No, no. I wanted the soft. Don't do that to me. Come on," said Ocon.

Source: Reuters

World

Starved residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky return to Ukraine during a rare local ceasefire

Reuters

31 October, 2026 08:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Olena Harmash and Anna Voitenko CHERNIHIV REGION, Ukraine, Oct 31 (Reuters) – Starved and exhausted residents from the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky crossed into Ukraine on Saturday in a major return of civilians under the first humanitarian truce of its kind in more than four years of the war.

The six-day local ceasefire in Oleshky was reached after mediation efforts by US first lady Melania Trump and with the pope’s involvement. It is the longest local pause in fighting since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

“As of now, Ukrainian citizens from Oleshky have crossed the Ukrainian border in the Chernihiv region. All of them will receive the assistance they need,” said President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, thanking the US and Melania Trump for mediation.

Show Full Article

Ukrainian officials greeted the evacuees with posters “You’re not alone” and “We embrace with our hearts.”

One elderly woman said that they had escaped from hell as she exited a bus. She was greeted by another woman wrapped in Ukraine’s national blue and yellow flag. Both cried.

To reach Ukrainian-held territory, Oleshky residents had to take a complicated route to leave the devastated town just a few kilometres away from the front line.

They first travelled by bus via Crimea to the Russian town of Anapa, before flying to Belarus from where they continued to Ukraine.

A video shared by Ukraine’s ombudsman showed dozens of Oleshky residents slowly disembarking from a plane at a Belarusian airfield. Many people were elderly. Some required help to walk, and a few were carried on stretchers or in wheelchairs. They carried minimal luggage – only a bag or two. Dogs were unloaded from the plane in cages.

BUSES WITH EVACUEES CROSS INTO UKRAINE

As several big buses crossed into Ukraine’s northern Chernihiv region from Belarus, the residents were greeted by relatives. Ambulances lined the street and several large military tents were erected where hot meals, tea and medical aid were provided.

Pet food and water bottles were piled up on several tables.

“We have come a complicated way: from negotiations and agreeing on a ceasefire to delivering humanitarian aid directly to Oleshky and organising the evacuation of civilians,” said Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman.

The ceasefire has been holding since Tuesday without violations, according to both Ukrainian and Russian officials. It has allowed them to de-mine the roads and bring food, medicines and other supplies into the town.

Supply routes to Oleshky were disrupted by fighting and drones. According to some residents, food deliveries were stopped in May, pushing hundreds of people into starvation.

The ceasefire will end on Sunday.

Lubinets said that the oldest returning resident was 94, while the youngest was a baby just over one. He gave no exact numbers on how many people returned to Ukraine.

Some residents decided to go to Russia, while others elected to remain in Oleshky, despite the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

Oleshky had a pre-war population of about 24,000. Before the evacuation, an estimated 1,700 remained. The town has been under Russian occupation since the first days of the invasion. It was devastated after the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam in 2023 and the flooding of the nearby areas.

FIGHTING RAGES ON IN OTHER PARTS OF THE FRONT

Despite the ceasefire on the southern Kherson front, fighting raged on in other parts of the front. Both Russia and Ukraine also kept up their drone attacks on each other.

Zelenskiy said that Russia attacked Ukrainian energy infrastructure, hitting electricity substations, thermal power plants and gas infrastructure.

Ukraine’s military said that it hit a major Russian producer of missile fuel in the Rostov region.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Ukrainian and Russian ombudsmen had a good dialogue and had gradually begun to trust each other as they worked together during the Oleshky ceasefire, Russia’s Vedomosti reported.

But the Kremlin said on Friday that it was an isolated situation, which was difficult to extrapolate to the broader peace process.

Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume talks in Abu Dhabi in early November after discussions were suspended in February following the outbreak of the war in Iran.

(Additional reporting by Valentyn Ogirenko, reporting by Reuters in Moscow and Kyiv; Editing by Joe Bavier and Alex Richardson)

Iranian envoys meet Qatari mediators as threat looms of US strikes after midterms

Reuters

31 October, 2026 08:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Andrew Mills, Yasmine Ghania and Enas Alashray DUBAI/CAIRO, Oct 31 (Reuters) – Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source told Reuters, as diplomats try to avert a new outbreak of fighting after the US midterm elections this week.

Saturday’s talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who was briefed on the negotiations and spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington.

Countries in the region have been anticipating that US President Donald Trump, who has held off on strikes on Iran during the weeks leading up to Tuesday’s midterm elections, could restart attacks once the voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

Show Full Article

Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.

“Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response,” Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since replacing his father slain at the war’s outset, said on Saturday in the statement posted on his official Telegram account.

He said that senior commanders had reported high readiness along the Gulf coast, in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and on Iran’s northwestern and southeastern borders.

DIPLOMACY CONTINUES DESPITE GAPS

Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election to keep his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can “finish the job”.

But Washington has also lately taken steps to indicate it is open to diplomacy. Earlier this week, Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation at previous rounds of talks with Iran, wrote a letter to a hardline senior Iranian security official, which the New York Times and Wall Street Journal described as an initiative to see if it was possible to restart talks.

Trump played the letter down, saying he approved it only to discuss the possibility of letting more medical supplies into Iran: “I said if you want to do that, that’s ok. Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well.”

In the latest Qatari-mediated discussions, the Qataris brought a proposal to Tehran a week ago for a seven-day plan, under which the US and Iran would take daily steps to build trust ahead of broader peace talks, the source briefed on the negotiations said. A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday that this proposal was not deemed satisfactory by Tehran.

Iran has been proposing its own seven-day plan since September, so far rejected by Trump. That calls for Washington to lift a blockade of Iranian ports, unfreeze assets and approve an Iranian-backed route through the Strait of Hormuz, after which the contested strait would be reopened.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in remarks reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday that Iran was studying Vance’s letter. He said the Iranian plan was the only proposal on the table to reopen the strait.

(Reporting by Andrew Mills, Enas Alashray and Yasmine Ghania, Writing by Andrew Mills; Editing by Peter Graff)

Oct 31 : Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday it has been able to replace 90 per cent of the amount stolen after a record $6.3 billion hack of its platform, by using company money to buy new tokens. The remaining 10 per cent consists of tokens that are less liquid, which means they may take longer to buy, it said in a statement posted on X. "We've now replenished 90 per cent of the stolen assets, and we're committed to covering the remaining 10 per cent. Our users will not bear the financial impact of this incident," co-CEO Richard Teng said on X on Saturday. Crypto prices fell on Friday, while Binance — the world's biggest crypto exchange — sought to reassure customers that their funds were safe after losing more than $6 billion worth of crypto in a hack which analysts blamed on North Korea.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a "complex attack" involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate. After the hack, the exchange stopped allowing customers to withdraw their funds, but it said on Saturday it was still on track to re-open withdrawals on Sunday. Binance said it has set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses.  The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures insurance fund, and the company's own corporate treasury, it said on X. LONDON, Oct 31 : The travelling fans applauded Michael Carrick when he strode to the corner of the Shed End at Stamford Bridge to acknowledge them but Manchester United's former stalwart midfielder and current manager cut a forlorn figure as he left the pitch after a 2-0 Premier League defeat by Chelsea on Saturday. A reckless challenge on Wesley Fofana midway through the second half earned Lisandro Martinez a sending off and Chelsea a penalty for their second goal, sealing United's fate in their ninth straight game without a win in all competitions. The United board decided to stick with Carrick for the Chelsea game despite a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last weekend and a 4-1 drubbing at Como in the Champions League. But the jubilant Chelsea crowd's rendition of "You'll be sacked in the morning" sounded increasingly portentous as he disappeared down the tunnel.

Carrick sidestepped questions about his future. "I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek," he said. United meet Roma at home in the Champions League on Tuesday. United, with captain Bruno Fernandes restored to the side after falling out with Carrick, looked lively in the first half but squandered a series of chances, notably from Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, who had a goal ruled offside, and Amad Diallo. Bryan Mbuemo also hit the post. "We didn't capitalise on the moments we had," Carrick said. "Second half got away from us... sometimes you get tough moments in the game and you have to deal with that." United were punished four minutes into the second half when Morgan Rogers picked up the ball just inside their half and cantered past a hesitant defence before delicately lifting it past goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Cole Palmer scored from the spot in the 63rd minute despite Lammens getting his hand to the ball as he dived to his right. "You give away a bad goal and it's a lot more challenging to be in that position with 10 men," Carrick said. He praised his players for their spirit of togetherness in a tough run of games, saying they had been "really tested but have stood by each other". The result means United could find themselves in the relegation zone by the end of the day. They are provisionally in 17th place, one point clear, while Chelsea have moved up to a provisional fourth. The London side have also suffered a disappointing week, losing 2-0 at home to London rivals Tottenham Hotspur last Saturday and to Liverpool away on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Manager Xabi Alonso chose to start spirited Brazil winger Estevao, 19, after criticism from fans that he was not being played enough and media rumours that he could leave the club. Estevao's trickery caused United problems and he had a goal disallowed for a tight offside call. "I'm very happy for him and he deserved to enjoy the game. He has a good connection with the crowd," Alonso said.

item.title: China pierde impulso económico en octubre ante contracción de la actividad industrial
item.description: El PMI manufacturero cayó a 49,3 en octubre, por debajo de las previsiones del mercado y del umbral que marca la expansión. La debilidad aumenta la presión sobre Pekín para impulsar la segunda mayor e ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La actividad industrial de China se ralentizó en octubre, lo que pone de relieve los retos a los que se enfrentan los responsables políticos en su intento por mantener la recuperación económica y garantizar que se alcance el objetivo de crecimiento de este año. El índice oficial de gestores de compras del sector manufacturero descendió hasta 49,3 desde el 50,1 registrado en septiembre, según informó el sábado la Oficina Nacional de Estadística. Este dato contrasta con la previsión media de 49,9 obtenida en una encuesta de Bloomberg a economistas. Una lectura superior a 50 indica expansión. Ver más: Marcas chinas superan a las japonesas en ventas de autos en Europa por primera vez El índice de actividad no manufacturera, que abarca la construcción y los servicios, se situó en 49,7, frente al 50,2 registrado en septiembre. Este deterioro sugiere que la segunda economía más grande del mundo ha perdido algo de impulso al inicio del cuarto trimestre, tras un modesto repunte en los tres meses anteriores. Pekín podría verse sometida a una mayor presión para ofrecer apoyo adicional tras haber introducido un nuevo paquete de medidas de estímulo específicas en las últimas semanas, ya que los responsables políticos tratan de mantener el crecimiento en la senda adecuada para cumplir el objetivo anual del gobierno, situado entre el 4,5% y el 5%. La debilidad se extendió tanto a la oferta como a la demanda: el índice de producción manufacturera cayó 1,9 puntos porcentuales hasta situarse en 49,8 y el indicador de nuevos pedidos descendió 1,1 puntos porcentuales hasta situarse en 49,4, según la oficina de estadística. Las grandes empresas manufactureras se mantuvieron en fase de expansión, con un índice de 50,2, mientras que los índices correspondientes a las medianas y pequeñas empresas descendieron hasta 48,4 y 47,5, respectivamente. El PMI del sector manufacturero de alta tecnología se situó en 51,3, registrando una expansión incluso cuando la actividad industrial global se contrajo. Ver más: “El financiamiento de China se ha replegado en el mundo”: estos son los desafíos para sus deudores en América Latina El gobierno ya ha intensificado las políticas destinadas a impulsar la economía, ofreciendo más apoyo crediticio a las pequeñas empresas y a los consumidores, subvenciones hipotecarias para algunos compradores de vivienda y cuotas adicionales de emisión de bonos para las administraciones locales. También se han puesto en marcha las obras de grandes proyectos de infraestructura, como el de las “Seis Redes”, y las autoridades han manifestado su disposición a introducir nuevas medidas si fuera necesario. -Con la c olaboración de Tian Ying. WASHINGTON: As the campaign for control of the US Congress reached its final weekend, the Trump administration stepped up its legal intervention in the Alaska Senate race while the number of Americans casting early ballots neared 50 million, a record for a midterm election. The Department of J us tice accelerated its criminal investigation in Alaska on Friday (Oct 30), following reports that aides to a Democratic Senate candidate recruited a retired schoolteacher from a remote fishing village to get on the ballot beca us e he has the same name as the Republican incumbent. The DOJ, acting on a civil lawsuit that US President Donald Trump said he instigated, also filed further motions in an attempt to block the state of Alaska from certifying the Senate results if the Republican incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, loses a close race on a ballot that includes the nonpartisan candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. The closely contested race in Alaska is seen as crucial for the Democrats if they hope to take control of the Senate from Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote. PROSECUTOR ALLEGES "SHAM CANDIDATE" IN KEY ALASKA RACE

It is one of 35 races in the 100-member Senate that will set the tone for Trump's final two years in office. Also up for grabs are all 435 seats in the US Ho us e of Representatives. Early voter participation this cycle has set a record. More than 49 million Americans have already cast ballots, either in person or by mail, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, up from nearly 46 million who voted before Election Day in the last midterms, in 2022. A Democratic victory in one or both chambers could result in congressional investigations of the Trump administration, which for two years has enjoyed largely compliant Republican majorities. Trump has been on a campaign blitz in multiple states over the past month but is not scheduled to travel on Saturday, when there will be a mash-up of American traditions: politics, Halloween and college football across the country. Trump returns to the campaign trail on Sunday in Kansas and Iowa. The DOJ's top prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said at a Friday press conference that a recent New York Times article about the supposed recruitment effort had driven a "surge" of FBI resources, adding that he had assigned several prosecutors to the case and that investigative steps were taking place "intensely and swiftly". The Times reported on Wednesday that aides to Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola recruited Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. to run. Heyman labelled him a "sham candidate" but declined to say what crime may have been committed. The department had already filed its civil action but, Heyman said, "when the New York Times article hit, that's additional information that accelerated what we've been doing". Peltola has denied knowing about any effort to recruit the second Sullivan. The retired teacher has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign .

Related:

Trump cancels weekend rallies, plans to phone in to other midterm campaign events

Beyond Trump: US midterms offer early test in battle for White House in 2028

ADMINISTRATION GETS INVOLVED IN RACES NATIONWIDE The Trump administration has also sued California to try to prevent the counting of ballots cast by more than 20,000 registered voters who the administration alleged could be noncitizens. It has also sued roughly 30 states and the District of Columbia, seeking unredacted voter rolls, part of a pattern that has alarmed election officials. A federal judge on Friday ordered the DOJ to stop threatening to prosecute California election officials who do not comply with the Trump administration's directives regarding alleged voting by noncitizens. Sean Morales-Doyle, director of the voting rights and elections program at the Brennan Center for J us tice, said the administration’s actions parallel the tactics undertaken by election deniers in the 2020 presidential election. While the administration is unlikely to win in court, he said, the efforts could create a political atmosphere that leads to official misconduct. “It's about creating uncertainty, sowing fear, distr us t, chaos, hoping that you create the political circumstances in which maybe the lieutenant governor of Alaska does feel pressure to do something that they're not supposed to do. Maybe the governor does start to question things, too,” Morales-Doyle said. Even so, a bipartisan majority of US voters tr us t the overall electoral process, with 76 per cent saying they are confident their ballots will be counted accurately, according to a Sep 30 to Oct 5 Reuters/Ipsos poll. Some 15 per cent were not confident and the rest were not sure or did not answer the question. Confidence was about equally high among Republicans and Democrats.

Source: Reuters/co

CAPE TOWN, Oct 31 : South Africa spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 and Kagiso Rabada became the fastest by balls bowled to reach 350 test wickets as the hosts thumped Australia by 176 runs to clinch their three-match series 2-1 at Newlands on Saturday. Set a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the test world rankings for the first time since January 2016. Australia had hopes of chasing down the total but lost two wickets in the first over of the final day and slumped to 62 for eight as their effort became a battle of survival that South Africa ended before tea. There will be questions asked of this Australia side in the wake of the defeat, not least another poor batting display and the decision to bowl on the opening morning that left them batting last on a wearing wicket.

"The trend of this game was once you got yourself in there were runs to be had," Australia captain Pat Cummins said. "But within the first hour the game was away from us and we did not give ourselves a chance. "We are a really good side but playing tough opponents away from home is always difficult. We came here thinking we were good enough to win but we couldn't do it." Hopes of victory evaporated in the first half hour as Rabada (3-39) removed the top three batters to take his tally to 350 test wickets, taking 13,808 deliveries, fewer than compatriot Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan’s Waqar Younis (14,905). After that Harmer came into his own, exploiting the conditions expertly to also claim a first 10-wicket haul in tests with figures of 10-120 across the match.   Rabada removed opener Matt Renshaw (0), caught by wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton down the leg side, and the struggling Marnus Labuschagne (4) leg before wicket in the first over of the innings He then had the dangerous Travis Head caught at gully by Marco Jansen to rock Australia early on. First-innings centurion Josh Inglis (4) was run out attempting a quick single to compound Australia’s woes, and from there Harmer took the last six wickets. Cummins (11 from 90 balls) and innings top-scorer Nathan Lyon (33 not out) delayed the inevitable with a ninth-wicket stand that lasted 17.2 overs, but Harmer trapped the former lbw and then bowled Josh Hazlewood to seal the win. "It was just understanding what I needed to do, getting the ball in the right areas as often as I could, and playing with my pace and trajectories, the little nuances I have learnt along the way. It all worked out alright," Harmer said. "Today was a lot of fun, fielders around the bat and trying to get the win. That is the stuff of dreams for a spinner."  The victory also keeps alive South Africa's hopes of defending their World Test Championship title next year having beaten Australia at Lord's in the previous decider in 2025.

item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 31 : US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centers.Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administrati

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 31 : US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centers. Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10 per cent since 2024 when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in both houses of the US Congress. Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services. Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.  Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry.

"It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers. "Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and they don't see any end in sight."  Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities’ requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity utilities can earn on their grid investments.  This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed.  Last year's spending was double the previous record. The investor-owned companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Global’s Regulatory Research Associates. UTILITIES SPOTLIGHTED Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia. Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not directly elected.  In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was "not beholden to utility companies" and work with the state attorney general to crack down on "excessive rate hikes and predatory practices." Ohio's residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20 per cent over the last two years, according to EIA data. Acton has also said she supports a data center moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all. BULLY PULPIT Some governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down. In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month. He followed up with a letter to more utility CEOs seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns on equity. "The governors are using this crisis on energy affordability as an opportunity to take a deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense," said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.  Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills. She did so the same day she took office. In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year’s elections.  Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid. "The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on the political calendar,” said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities. “It requires consistent investment every year to deliver reliable energy to our customers." Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits. For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households. "I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Residents of Russian-controlled Ukrainian town arrive in Belarus
item.description: Hundreds of starving and exhausted residents left the town of Oleshky on Friday during a US-backed local ceasefire, the first of its kind and the longest humanitarian pause in the war, which is nearing its fifth year.
item.dc:creator: CNA

World

Residents of Russian-controlled Ukrainian town arrive in Belarus

Hundreds of starving and exhausted residents left the town of Oleshky on Friday during a US-backed local ceasefire, the first of its kind and the longest humanitarian pause in the war, which is nearing its fifth year.

People attend an evacuation from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in the Kherson region, in this handout picture released Oct 30, 2026. Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, Kyrylo Budanov/Handout via Reuters

31 Oct 2026 05:59PM

FAST

KYIV: Four planes carrying residents evacuated from the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky landed in Belarus on Saturday (Oct 31), the Belarusian Belta state news agency and a senior Ukrainian official said. Hundreds of starving and exhausted residents left the town of Oleshky on Friday during a US-backed local ceasefire, the first of its kind and the longest humanitarian pause in the war, which is nearing its fifth year. "The last, fourth plane landed in Gomel," said David Arakhamia, a top Ukrainian peace negotiator and close ally of President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. "In a few hours, all Ukrainian citizens evacuated from Oleshky together with a Ukrainian delegation will be on Ukrainian territory."

Belta later reported that a convoy of buses carrying the residents had departed from the airport in Gomel, in southeastern Belarus near the border with Ukraine. The evacuees leaving for Ukraine had to take a complicated route to leave Oleshky as the frontline runs just a few kilometres away. They first travelled by bus via Crimea to the Russian town of Anapa before flying to Belarus from where they will continue to Ukraine via a border crossing, Belta said. The local ceasefire in Oleshky was reached thanks to mediation efforts by US first lady Melania Trump and with the pope's involvement. The ceasefire has been holding since Tuesday without violations, according to both Ukrainian and Russian officials. It has allowed them to de-mine the roads and bring food, medicines and other supplies into the town. Supply routes to Oleshky were disrupted by fighting and drones. According to some residents, food deliveries were stopped in May, pushing hundreds of people into starvation. It was not immediately clear how many people decided to leave Oleshky and how many opted to stay in the town. Oleshky residents had options to travel to Russia or to return to Ukraine. Ukrainian officials have said around 1,700 people remained in Oleshky from a pre-war population of about 24,000. According to several residents interviewed by Reuters, many of those were elderly or ill.

Source: Reuters/kl

item.title: Pakistan military 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
item.description: Pakistan's chief mediator in its efforts to de-escalate the now eight-month-old Iran war has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Asia

Pakistan military 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation

Pakistan's chief mediator in its efforts to de-escalate the now eight-month-old Iran war has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei attend a meeting with Chief of Defence Forces of Pakistan, Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin in Tehran, Iran, October 26, 2026. Iran's Presidential website/WANA (West Asia News Agency)/Handout via REUTERS

FAST

RAWALPINDI: Pakistan’s military is “cautiously optimistic” about its mediation between Iran and the United States, its spokesman said on Friday (Oct 30) in his first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week. Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir - Pakistan's chief mediator in its efforts to de-escalate the now eight-month-old Iran war - has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials. “Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive sign. “The word that we would use is always cautiously optimistic,” added Chaudhry, director general of Inter-Services Public Relations.

There were still "powerful spoilers and detractors" who believed conflict serves them, he added without naming them. Speaking in the garrison city of Rawalpindi, where Pakistan's armed forces are headquartered, Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed or whether the United States had backed the trip. Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin joined Munir in Tehran on Monday. Their two countries signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan on Aug 7, saying an attack on any signatory will be treated as an attack on all. The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement has taken on added significance as the Iran war has redrawn regional alliances and raised fears of a broader Middle East conflict. While the three signatories say the agreement is aimed at collective deterrence and regional security, analysts see its evolution as closely tied to efforts by regional powers to manage the fallout from the Iran-US confrontation. After Monday’s talks, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said regional security should be ensured by regional countries without foreign intervention. The wording of the pact does not bar new members, Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join. “Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide. Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership. He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi Arabia and the holy sites of Mecca and Medina. "We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an intra-Yemen conflict," he added. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group has been reignited by the Iran conflict, stoking fears of a wider war. HOME FRONT On the home front, the federal government suspended the provincial government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), on Oct 11 and detained Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. The government had accused the provincial administration of failing to tackle militancy. The PTI rejected the allegations and says its government took part in counter-terrorism efforts. PTI leaders called the move a pretext to crush protests. Asked if there would now be larger military-led campaigns in the province, Chaudhry said that was not how the army conducted counter-terrorism. "Our counter-terrorism operations are based on what we call IBOs, intelligence-based operations ... The tempo of the freedom of action of (those) IBOs will further increase," he said. Independents backed by Khan’s PTI won the most directly elected seats in the February 2024 election but fell short of a majority. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was the only province controlled by Khan’s party. Khan has been in jail since 2023, and his supporters see the military behind his imprisonment and the dismantlement of the PTI. The army denies involvement in politics.

Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say

item.title: Hong Kong telecom company agrees to halt US operations under pressure
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission has previously barred China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States, citing broad national security concerns.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Hong Kong telecom company agrees to halt US operations under pressure

The Federal Communications Commission has previously barred China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States, citing broad national security concerns.

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) seal decorates a wall inside their headquarters in Washington, D.C., U.S., Jul 22, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Kylie Cooper)

FAST

WASHINGTON: HKT, a leading Hong Kong telecom carrier and subsidiary of PCCW Ltd, on Friday (Oct 30) agreed to halt its operations in the United States under pressure from the Federal Communications Commission. The FCC in October 2025 said it was moving to revoke the authority of HKT to operate in the United States, citing national security concerns and its affiliation with China Unicom, which is a shareholder in PCCW. Under a consent decree reviewed by Reuters, HKT has agreed to stop international and domestic telecom services to and within the United States. HKT must file an application with the FCC within 30 days to discontinue services and must discontinue US services by September 1, 2027. PCCW declined immediate comment. The agreement means the FCC will not move forward with the revocation proceeding that could have offered more details on Washington's national security concerns.

The FCC has previously barred China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States, citing broad national security concerns. The Trump administration has continued an extensive crackdown on Chinese telecoms over the past year. The FCC on Thursday voted to ban all Chinese labs from testing US electronics starting from December 2028. The telecom crackdown has sparked a strong reaction from Beijing. China said Friday it firmly opposes the FCC action on labs, warning it would take necessary countermeasures "if the US side persists in acting unilaterally". The FCC also announced on Thursday it plans to soon ban Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers on national security grounds. The plan would bar Chinese IP network service providers from direct access and those that use equipment from companies on the FCC's list that pose national security risks, including Huawei and ZTE. Other measures under consideration by the FCC include barring Chinese telecom firms from connecting to US networks and from operating their data centers in the US.  Concerns about the potential for spying and other harms to arise from Chinese access to US telecom data and infrastructure have grown in recent years. In late 2024, Washington said a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group known as Salt Typhoon stole consumers' call records and US call data and infiltrated US telecommunications and telecom infrastructure firms. China has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

item.title: Chinese-Founded Nigerian Fintech Giant OPay Scraps $304 Million U.S. IPO Amid Regulatory Probe
item.description: SoftBank-backed digital-payments company OPay withdrew a planned $304 million U.S. initial public offering on Friday, citing a regulatory inquiry by a foreign jurisdiction it did not identify. The Nigeria-focused company described the inquiry as relating to a jurisdiction “immaterial” to its core operations. In a …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
SoftBank-backed digital-payments company OPay withdrew a planned $304 million U.S. initial public offering on Friday, citing a regulatory inquiry by a foreign jurisdiction it did not identify.

The Nigeria-focused company described the inquiry as relating to a jurisdiction “immaterial” to its core operations. In a statement, it did not identify the regulator or nature of the inquiry.

OPay said it expected the matter to be resolved satisfactorily in the near future and that the probe “should not be misconstrued as a reflection on the Company’s business performance, financial condition, operational integrity, or regulatory standing.”

The company said the inquiry would not affect its operations, regulatory standing or customer service in Nigeria or its other markets.

OPay could not immediately be reached for comment outside office hours.

Earlier in the day, OPay said it had priced 16 million American depositary shares at $19 each, the bottom of its targeted $19-to-$21 range, valuing the company at about $4 billion.

Japanese tech investor SoftBank Group 9984.T, whose entities owned a 6.6% stake in OPay before the offering, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Numerous companies worldwide have delayed stock market listings in recent weeks as stubborn inflation and a selloff in AI-related stocks have weighed on investor sentiment.

OPay, founded in 2018, provides digital financial services across emerging markets, including Nigeria and Indonesia.

Its app offers payments, money transfers, savings and loans in economies where limited access to traditional banking can make everyday transactions difficult.

OPay was founded by Chinese billionaire Yahui Zhou, who also founded Beijing Kunlun Tech, a Chinese gaming company that previously owned dating app Grindr.

The fintech raised $400 million in 2021 at a valuation of $2 billion. It had about 50 million monthly active users as of July 31, according to its IPO prospectus.

Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, Standard Bank and CICC were among the underwriters. The company had planned to list on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “OPay.”

China's factory activity marks third contraction in four months

FAST

BEIJING: China's factory activity unexpectedly dropped in October, its third contraction in four months, a government survey showed on Saturday (Oct 31), hurt by soft demand for exports as well as goods at home. The official manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics. That missed a forecast for 50.0 from a Reuters poll. Factory activity weakened as overseas Christmas-related orders, which were front-loaded in September, cooled in October. It was also hurt when consumer spending, which climbed during China's long National Day holiday in the first week of October, fizzled out after, in a return to its long-stagnant state. "Insufficient demand is increasing downward pressure on the economy," said Zhang Liqun, an analyst with the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, adding that policymakers should take the problem seriously and step up measures as soon as possible.

Sub-indexes for new orders overall and for new export orders both stayed in contraction territory in October. Production and purchasing activity also slipped into contraction from expansion. The non-manufacturing PMI, which covers services and construction, also dropped to 49.7 from 50.2 in September. The readings are compiled based on purchasing managers' reports about whether conditions improved, worsened or were unchanged in areas such as new orders, output and employment compared with the previous month. A reading above 50 signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction. Some sectors within manufacturing were doing well. Production and new orders sub-indexes for railway, shipbuilding, aerospace equipment, and computer, communications and electronics manufacturing were all at or above 53.0, the survey showed. AI-related firms in particular have reported strong earnings growth. Zhongji Innolight, a maker of high-speed optical modules that connect servers and switches in AI data centres, posted a near tripling in third-quarter net profit. But the lacklustre domestic market and rising costs have weighed on many old-school manufacturers and property-linked firms. Custom furniture maker Oppein Home, for example, saw net profit plunge 80 per cent during the quarter. China's economy is, however, expected to meet the country's 4.5-5.0 per cent annual growth target without additional stimulus measures after third-quarter growth rebounded to 4.5 per cent from 4.3 per cent in April-June.

Source: Reuters/kl

item.title: 中国製造業ＰＭＩ、10月は49.3 4カ月で3度目の縮小
item.description: [北京 ３１日 ロイター] - 中国国家統計局が３１日発表した１０月の製造業購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は４９．３に低下...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国製造業ＰＭＩ、10月は49.3　4カ月で3度目の縮小 10/31 12:54 配信

写真は中国広東省東莞市にある工場倉庫で３月撮影。 REUTERS/Tingshu Wang（ロイター） [北京 ３１日 ロイター] - 中国国家統計局が３１日発表した１０月の製造業購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は４９．３に低下し、景気拡大と縮小の分岐点となる５０を下回った。製造業活動が縮小したのは過去４カ月で３度目。国内の財需要の低迷と輸出の弱まりの兆しが重しとなった。

ロイターがまとめた市場予想の５０．０を下回った。９月は５０．１だった。

製造業活動が弱まったのは、９月に前倒しされていた海外からのクリスマス関連受注が１０月になって落ち着いたため。国慶節の大型連休中に増加した個人消費も、連休明けには勢いを失い、長期の低迷状態に戻ったことが響いた。

中国物流購買連合会のアナリスト張立群氏は「需要不足が景気への下押し圧力を強めている」と指摘。政策当局はこの問題を深刻に受け止め、できるだけ早く対策を強化すべきだと述べた。

新規受注指数と新規輸出受注指数はいずれも縮小圏にとどまった。生産と購買活動も拡大から縮小に転じた。

ピンポイント・アセット・マネジメントのチーフエコノミスト張智威氏は、２０２７年に外需が弱まれば「中国は内需を押し上げるため、より大規模な政策支援が必要になる」と述べた。

東呉証券のチーフエコノミスト、ルー・ジャー氏は「家計の信頼感を支え、心理を安定させるため」、住宅ローン利払いへの補助拡充が必要だとした。また、利払いへの補助を投資事業にも広げれば、採算の見込める固定資産投資案件が不足している現状の緩和につながるとの見方を示した。

サービス業と建設業を対象とする非製造業ＰＭＩも４９．７と、９月の５０．２から低下した。

ＰＭＩは、新規受注や生産、雇用などの状況が前月と比べて改善したか、悪化したか、変わらなかったかについて、購買担当者の回答を基に算出する。５０を上回ると活動の拡大、下回ると縮小を示す。

製造業の一部業種は好調だった。鉄道、造船、航空宇宙機器やコンピューター・通信・電子機器の製造業では、生産指数と新規受注指数がいずれも５３．０以上となった。

特に人工知能（ＡＩ）関連企業は大幅な増益を報告している。ＡＩデータセンターでサーバーとスイッチを接続する高速光モジュールを製造する中際旭創（ジョンジー・イノライト）は、第３・四半期の純利益が約３倍となった。

一方、国内市場の低迷とコスト上昇は、多くの従来型の製造業や不動産関連企業の重しとなっている。オーダーメード家具メーカーの欧派家居（オッペイン・ホーム）は、同期の純利益が８０％減少した。

ただ、中国経済は第３・四半期の成長率が４．５％と、４─６月期の４．３％から持ち直したことから、追加の景気刺激策なしでも年間４．５─５．０％の成長目標を達成する見通しだ。

ロイター 関連リンク コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：経済モデル転換目指す中国、不動産不況でも資源需要衰えず コラム：「カメ」の米国株が「ウサギ」の中国を追い抜く時 10/31(土) 14:27 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝八村が復帰戦で12得点、クリッパーズは黒星 ＮＢＡカップ
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は３０日、シーズン中のトーナメント戦であるＮＢＡカップを各地で行い、八村塁が所属する西カンファレンスＢ組のクリッパーズはティンバーウルブズに１０１─１２７で敗れて黒星発進となった。

左太ももの痛みで２８日のレーカーズ戦を欠場していた八村が先発で復帰。２６分２２秒の出場で３点シュート２本を含む１２得点、５リバウンド、２スチールを記録した。クリッパーズはダリアス・ガーランドがチーム最多の２４得点をマーク。チームはターンオーバー数で相手の１１回に対して１７回を記録し、公式戦４連敗となった。

Ａ組では、マーベリックスがロケッツに１１６─１１１で競り勝った。カイリー・アービングが３５得点、クーパー・フラッグが３３得点とチームをけん引した。

東カンファレンスでは、Ｂ組のセブンティシクサーズが昨季王者のニックスに９８─９３で競り勝った。タイリース・マクシーがチーム最多の２７得点に、先発したレブロン・ジェームズも２０得点、９リバウンド、８アシストと存在感を示した。

Ａ組では、マジックがラプターズに１２１─１１４で勝利。ピストンズはネッツを１１０─９４で下した。Ｃ組のセルティックスはブルズに１２５─１１１で快勝した。

item.title: サッカー＝プリシッチ、ミランと新契約を締結 31年まで
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイタリア・セリエＡ、ＡＣミランは３０日、米国代表ＭＦクリスティアン・プリシッチ（２８）と２０３１年までの新契約を締結したと発表した。

２３年にミラン入りしたプリシッチは、同クラブで通算１４１試合に出場し、４４ゴール２８アシストを記録。２７年６月までとなっていた契約を延長し、３０年ワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）以降もミランでプレーすることになった。

プリシッチはクラブ公式の交流サイトを通じて、「ミランは私に全てを与えてくれた。ここは自分の家のようだ。このクラブを心から愛している」と述べた。

これまでチェルシー（イングランド）やドルトムント（ドイツ）でプレーした経験を持つプリシッチは、米国代表として９０試合に出場して３３得点を記録。２２年Ｗ杯と２６年Ｗ杯にも出場し、米国サッカー連盟が選出する年間最優秀男子選手賞を過去４回受賞している。

item.title: ゴルフ＝平田が2位を維持、中島は20位に浮上 メキシコＯＰ
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフの秋季シリーズ、メキシコ・オープンは３０日、メキシコのビダンタ・バジャルタ（パー７１）で第２ラウンドを行い、平田憲聖が２位を維持した。

平田は３バーディー、ノーボギーの６８とスコアを伸ばし、通算１１アンダーの１３１で首位と３打差につけている。

前日３５位の中島啓太は６バーディー、１ボギーの６６をマークし、通算８アンダーの１３４で２０位に浮上した。金谷拓実は予選落ちした。

アンドルー・ノバク（米国）が６１と猛チャージを見せ、通算１４アンダーの１２８で単独首位に浮上。平田ら５人が２位で並んだ。

item.title: 習主席、訪中のドイツ大統領と会談 友好的な貿易政策要請
item.description:
Mei Mei Chu Liz Lee
[北京 ３０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Mei Mei Chu　Liz Lee

[北京 ３０日 ロイター] - 中国の習近平国家主席は３０日、ドイツのシュタインマイヤー大統領と北京で会談し、「理性的で実務的かつ友好的」な対中政策を取るよう求めた。欧州との貿易摩擦が強まる中、平等や互恵、戦略的安定に基づく「全方位的な戦略パートナーシップ」を支持する考えを示した。

習氏は「この新たな関係のあり方は、われわれが閉鎖よりも開放を、対立よりも協力を支持するという前向きなシグナルを世界に送るものだ」とシュタインマイヤー氏に語った。

シュタインマイヤー氏は欧州連合（ＥＵ）が拡大する対中貿易赤字への対応を強める中、５日間の日程で中国を訪問。前日には、中国の経済的自立に向けた取り組みが他の市場を犠牲にしてはならないと警告していた。独仏は、ＥＵに損害を与える国に迅速に対抗する新措置を提案し、中国を念頭に置いているとみられる。

中国はスイスとの自由貿易協定改定やアイスランドとの航空路線新設など、欧州への外交攻勢を展開している。ただ、ＳＯＡＳ中国研究所のスティーブ・ツァン所長は、自国の経済利益を優先する中国の姿勢に対する懸念を和らげる効果は限定的と指摘。従来、中国との緊密な経済関係を推進してきたドイツ産業界からも、対中政策の厳格化を求める声が強まっていると述べた。

item.title: オープンＡＩ、資金調達目標を100億ドル引き下げ＝ＦＴ
item.description: [３０日 ロイター] - 英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）は３０日、米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業オープンＡＩが最新の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
オープンＡＩ、資金調達目標を100億ドル引き下げ＝ＦＴ 10/31 10:23 配信

写真はオープンＡＩのロゴ。６月撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） [３０日 ロイター] - 英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）は３０日、米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業オープンＡＩが最新の資金調達ラウンドの目標額を１００億ドル引き下げ、企業評価額１兆２５００億ドルで２００億ドルの調達を目指していると報じた。事情に詳しい関係者の話として伝えた。

対話型ＡＩ「チャットＧＰＴ」を手がける同社は当初、企業評価額１兆４０００億ドルで３００億ドルを調達する計画だった。ロイターは先週、競合するアンソロピックが１１月中旬に予定する株式上場を前に、オープンＡＩが投資家の出資取り付けを急いでいると報じていた。

ＦＴによると、オープンＡＩは投資家が出資を確約する期限を３０日に設定した。ただ、一部の投資家が出資額を減らしたため、第１段階の調達額は２００億ドルを下回る見通しだという。

オープンＡＩからコメントは得られていない。

ＡＩへの巨額支出に対する懸念の高まりを受け、３０日の米国株式市場では米ハイテク株が急落。ナスダック総合指数は２．９％安となり、１０月６日に付けた終値ベースの最高値から７．８％下落している。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：米ビックテック決算「現金が王様」、ＡＩ投資の成算に厳しい視線 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か 10/31(土) 10:23 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: Ｆ１＝メキシコＧＰフリー走行、ルクレール最速 岩佐と平川が参加
item.description: ［メキシコ市 ３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［メキシコ市　３０日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の今季第１９戦、メキシコ・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は３０日、メキシコ市でフリー走行を行い、フェラーリのシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）がこの日のトップタイムを記録した。

フリー走行１回目に最速１分１８秒１２８を記録したルクレールは、２回目でトップタイムの１分１７秒８２７をマークした。

２９日のメディア対応を体調不良のため欠席していたメルセデスのキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア）は１回目で２番手、２回目で４番手だった。個人総合でチームメートのジョージ・ラッセル（英国）に１２３点差をつけて首位に立つアントネッリは、今回のメキシコＧＰで９位以内に入ればＦ１史上最年少王者となる。

マクラーレンのランド・ノリス（英国）は２回目でルクレールと０秒１０３差の２番手。ラッセルは３番手だった。

残り４７分には、レッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）とレーシングブルズのリアム・ローソン（ニュージーランド）が接触。フェルスタッペンのマシンの破片がコース上に散乱し、赤旗で一時中断となった。

フェラーリのルイス・ハミルトン（英国）は残り３０分でマシンをコース上にストップさせ、バーチャル・セーフティーカーが導入。ハミルトンは無線で「完全にパワーを失った」と報告した。

また、１回目には岩佐歩夢（レッドブル）、平川亮（ハース）の日本人ドライバーが参加し、それぞれ５番手の１分１９秒１１３、１５番手の１分１９秒９８２のタイムを残した。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝モラントが左太もも裏負傷、最低4週間離脱へ 古巣戦で負傷
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のトレイルブレーザーズは３０日、ガードのジャ・モラント（２７）が左太もも裏の肉離れで最低４週間離脱すると発表した。

モラントは２９日に行われた古巣グリズリーズとの試合で負傷。ＭＲＩ検査の結果、グレード２の肉離れが判明した。４週間後に再検査を受ける予定という。

モラントは第４クオーターで途中退場。この試合では２３分間の出場で１４得点、３アシストを記録した。トレイルブレーザーズは１０３─１２４で敗れ、開幕からの連勝が３で止まった。

今季からトレイルブレーザーズでプレーするモラントは、ここまで４試合に出場し、１試合平均１５．８得点、５．５アシストを記録している。

モラントは２０１９年のドラフト全体２位でグリズリーズに入団。１９─２０年シーズンに新人王、２１─２２年シーズンには最も成長を見せた選手に贈られる賞を受賞し、オールスターにも２回選出された。

一方、けがや銃に関連した問題による出場停止処分などもあった。６月２９日にトレードでトレイルブレーザーズへ移籍した。

item.title: 再送Ｇ２０外相会合、ロシア参加に欧州反発 米長官は協力促す
item.description:
(見出しを修正しました)
Andrea Shalal
[アトランタ（米ジョージア州） ３０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
(見出しを修正しました)

Andrea Shalal

[アトランタ（米ジョージア州） ３０日 ロイター] - ２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）外相会合が３０日、米ジョージア州アトランタで開幕した。ルビオ米国務長官は、地政学的な安定と経済的繁栄の拡大に向けた協力を呼びかけ、一連の危機が世界の経済秩序を脅かしていると警告した。

ただ、ルビオ氏の招待によるロシアのラブロフ外相の参加に多くの外相が反発し、ウクライナと中東の戦争を巡る溝が深まった。会合は共同宣言を採択せず、議長声明を発表して閉幕する見通しだ。

英国のミリバンド外相はラブロフ氏に直接、ロシアの無人機攻撃で前日に１５人が死亡したと指摘し、「あなた方が侵略者であることは、われわれ全員が分かっている」と非難。ラブロフ氏は、ウクライナがロシアの安全保障上の脅威となることは容認できないと述べた。

欧州側がラブロフ氏との写真撮影を拒んだため、恒例の集合写真は見送られた。西側外交官によると、豪州やカナダを含むメンバーの３分の１が撮影に反対した。

また西側当局者らによると、中東の戦争がもたらす経済的課題の深刻さについては、おおむね認識が一致。多くの出席者は、米国によるイラン攻撃が再開すれば、原油価格が急騰して打撃が深まると懸念を示した。

外相らは３１日、供給網（サプライチェーン）や重要鉱物の調達について協議する予定。米中の戦略的競争も合意形成を難しくしている。１２月１４─１６日にマイアミで開く首脳会議での共同宣言採択に向け、調整が続く。

欧州連合（ＥＵ）のカラス外交安全保障上級代表は、ウクライナ支援拡大とロシアの責任追及を求める考えを示した。

item.title: ゴルフ＝山下が単独首位浮上、メイバンク選手権で連覇へ前進
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのメイバンク選手権は３０日、マレーシアのクアラルンプール・クラブ（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、昨年覇者の山下美夢有が単独首位に浮上した。

２位スタートの山下美夢有は６バーディー、ノーボギーの６６をマークし、通算１３アンダーの１３１とした。２位勢に２打差をつけ、２連覇と米ツアー今季３勝目に向けて好位置につけた。

前日２１位で出た吉田優利は７０、同１２位の岩井明愛は７１で回り、ともに通算５アンダーの２３位となった。そのほかの日本勢は、勝みなみが３９位、岩井千怜と渋野日向子が４６位、原英莉花と古江彩佳が５３位だった。

首位で出たポーリーヌ・ルサンブシャール（フランス）は６９で回り、通算１１アンダーの２位。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝マーリンズ、元サイ・ヤング賞アルカンタラの契約オプション行使
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のマーリンズは３０日、サンディ・アルカンタラ投手（３１）との契約に関し、２０２７年年俸２１００万ドル（約３３億円）の球団オプションを行使した。

マーリンズがオプションを行使しない場合、２００万ドルの契約解除金を支払う必要があった。

アルカンタラは今季３６試合（先発３３試合）に登板し、１３勝１１敗３セーブ、防御率３．８７、１５３三振を記録。投球回２１４はメジャー最多だった。

マーリンズのピーター・ベンディックス編成本部長はシーズン終了時の記者会見で、「サンディは球団にとって非常に大きな存在。今季も素晴らしいシーズンだった」と称賛。さらに、チーム内でのリーダーシップや模範的な振る舞いについて「他に並ぶものがない」と高く評価した。

アルカンタラは１７年にカージナルスでメジャーデビューし、通算２１３試合（先発２０２試合）に登板して６５勝７８敗、防御率３．６９。２２年にナ・リーグのサイ・ヤング賞（最優秀投手賞）を受賞したが、右肘のトミー・ジョン手術により２４年シーズンを全休した。

item.title: サッカー＝ルアーブル瀬古と中村先発もＰＳＧに大敗、マインツ佐野は終盤までプレー
item.description: ［３０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３０日　ロイター］ - サッカーのフランス１部は３０日、各地でリーグ戦を行い、瀬古歩夢と中村草太が先発したルアーブルはホームのパリ・サンジェルマン戦に１─５で大敗した。

前半１８分に先制したルアーブルだが、同２６分に追いつかれると、その後アクラフ・ハキミにハットトリックを許すなどさらに４失点して大敗した。瀬古はフル出場、中村は後半２０分までプレーした。チームメートの水多海斗はベンチスタートから出番がなかった。

上田綺世が所属するリールはホームにＲＣランスを迎え、後半４１分にオリビエ・ジルーが決勝点を記録し、１─０で勝利。負傷中の上田はメンバー外だった。

ドイツ１部ブンデスリーガでは、マインツの佐野海舟が敵地のエルファースベルク戦で先発し、後半４２分までプレー。チームは１─４で敗れた。

item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Crypto exchanges call for quick moves to bolster defenses after Binance heist

FAST

Oct 30 : Crypto exchanges are taking quick action to bolster their defenses and urging greater industry-wide information-sharing after a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance exposed their vulnerability just as they become more embedded in mainstream finance. Coinbase said it made adjustments to its systems that store cryptocurrency keys offline "solely out of an abundance of caution," while Kraken said it was monitoring industry incidents for lessons it could apply to its defenses. But the industry will need to move urgently, analysts and industry executives said, as President Donald Trump's regulators promote deeper integration of digital assets into the financial system, raising the stakes for an industry with a history of big hacks. "For crypto to reach its full potential, the security situation must be addressed immediately," said Chris Perkins, Franklin Templeton's head of crypto.
